newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Construction of Indonesian deepwater port launched.
newsitem.headline: Construction of Indonesian deepwater port launched.

text.p: Indonesia's PT Bina Jasa Hantarindo, controlled by President Suharto's son Bambang Trihatmodjo, has started construction of a deepwater port in West Java, The Jakarta Post reported on Friday.
The port, with an initial investment of $700 million, is located in Bojonegara, West Java, and is expected to ease the burden on Jakarta's crowded Tanjung Priok port, it said.
Another company, controlled by Suharto's son Hutomo Mandala Putra, is currently building a third container terminal in Tanjung Priok.

The Bojonegoro port was expected to be able to accommodate the latest generation of container ships which have a draft of up to 18 metres and a capacity of over 6,000 twenty-feet equivalent units (TEUs) and start operating in 1998.
